memory_lessons.applicability: This candidate keeps the 128-thread CTA and compact source representation while changing the tile length, making it a useful follow-up comparison.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 128-thread/128-source compact-tile candidate averaged 0.000899768 seconds, versus 0.001011208 seconds for the 256-thread/256-source compact tile and 0.001003741 seconds for the 256-thread full-particle tile. These results compare tested configurations and do not isolate tile length as the cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 128-thread, 256-source compact tile with the official correctness suite and timing metric.

proposal.hypothesis: The best measured T1 candidate used a 128-thread CTA with a 128-source compact tile. Keeping that CTA and target mapping while doubling only the source tile to 256 may halve tile-loop and barrier iterations; the larger 4096-byte shared-memory allocation may offset that benefit, so timing must decide.

retained: Keep the 128-thread CTA and matching 128-item launch mapping, and configure 4096 bytes of dynamic shared memory for a 256-entry compact source tile.
Have the CTA cooperatively stage each bounded source chunk, synchronize before its reuse and before replacing it, and let each active thread accumulate one target's force across the chunk.
Keep inactive tail threads participating in every barrier; exclude self-interactions by global source index and write each valid target once, preserving the original integration and particle mass.
